author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That we ought to lay open our necessities to Christ and to require His Grace

verses.text: O most sweet and loving Lord, whom now I devoutly desire to receive, Thou knowest my infirmity and the necessity which I suffer, in what evils and vices I lie; how often I am weighed down, tempted, disturbed, and defiled.
verses.modernizedText: O most sweet and loving Lord, whom now I devoutly desire to receive, You know my infirmity and the necessity which I suffer, in what evils and vices I lie; how often I am weighed down, tempted, disturbed, and defiled.

verses.text: I come unto Thee for remedy, I beseech of Thee consolation and support.
verses.modernizedText: I come to You for remedy, I beseech of You consolation and support.

verses.text: I speak unto Thee who knowest all things, to whom all my secrets are open, and who alone art able perfectly to comfort and help me.
verses.modernizedText: I speak to You who know all things, to whom all my secrets are open, and who alone are able perfectly to comfort and help me.

verses.text: Thou knowest what good thing I most stand in need of, and how poor I am in virtues.
verses.modernizedText: You know what good thing I most need, and how poor I am in virtues.

verses.text: Behold, I stand poor and naked before Thee, requiring grace, and imploring mercy.
verses.modernizedText: Behold, I stand poor and naked before You, requiring grace, and imploring mercy.

verses.text: Refresh the hungry suppliant, kindle my coldness with the fire of Thy love, illuminate my blindness with the brightness of Thy presence.
verses.modernizedText: Refresh the hungry suppliant, kindle my coldness with the fire of Your love, illuminate my blindness with the brightness of Your presence.

verses.text: Turn thou all earthly things into bitterness for me, all grievous and contrary things into patience, all things worthless and created into contempt and oblivion.
verses.modernizedText: Turn all earthly things into bitterness for me, all grievous and contrary things into patience, all things worthless and created into contempt and oblivion.

verses.text: Lift up my heart unto Thee in Heaven, and suffer me not to wander over the earth.
verses.modernizedText: Lift up my heart to You in Heaven, and do not allow me to wander over the earth.

verses.text: Be Thou alone sweet unto me from this day forward for ever, because Thou alone art my meat and drink, my love and joy, my sweetness and my whole good.
verses.modernizedText: Be alone sweet to me from this day forward forever, because You alone are my food and drink, my love and joy, my sweetness and my whole good.

verses.text: Oh that Thou wouldest altogether by Thy presence, kindle, consume, and transform me into Thyself; that I may be made one spirit with Thee, by the grace of inward union, and the melting of earnest love!
verses.modernizedText: Oh that You would altogether by Your presence kindle, consume, and transform me into Yourself; that I may be made one spirit with You, by the grace of inward union, and the melting of earnest love!

verses.text: Suffer me not to go away from Thee hungry and dry; but deal mercifully with me, as oftentimes Thou hast dealt wondrously with Thy saints.
verses.modernizedText: Do not allow me to go away from You hungry and dry; but deal mercifully with me, as often You have dealt wondrously with Your saints.

verses.text: What marvel if I should be wholly kindled from Thee, and in myself should utterly fail, since Thou art fire always burning and never failing, love purifying the heart and enlightening the understanding.
verses.modernizedText: What marvel if I should be wholly kindled from You, and in myself should utterly fail, since You are fire always burning and never failing, love purifying the heart and enlightening the understanding.
